title: Execution-equality expected result (fixture expectedRows.json shape)
description: T-1b's oracle: the rows the fixture's compiled query MUST return over the fixture's dataset.json, on every backend that can run it, compared under XEQ-3 in spec/semantics.md. Hand-derived from the semantics, never copied from an engine run: an oracle taken from the implementation it grades only proves the implementation agrees with itself. One shape serves an ungrouped page, a grouped level and a drill-down leaf alike: `columns` is the LOGICAL column list in result order (an ordinary row query: every schema field in declaration order, GRP-3's leaf rule; a grouped level: GRP-3's group column then each aggregation's `valueCols` entry `id`, never the compiled key; an export is never a grouped level, EXP-1(a); a BM-3 values query or an export: its own list), with each engine's rows mapped onto it by the harness (XEQ-3) and `rows` are ordered cell lists aligned to it. Order is part of the contract: SEM-6's stableKey tiebreaker makes every result order total. Rows are the page the request's startRow/endRow selects, not the whole match set. Cell encodings follow XEQ-2.

cell.description: One cell. A decimal is a JSON string carrying its exact digits; a date or datetime is a string; a missing value is an explicit null (XEQ-2).

columns.description: The logical column names the result carries, in result order.

rows.description: The result rows in result order. May be empty: an empty page is a legitimate, discriminating answer (a filter that must match nothing).

items.description: One row, one cell per entry of `columns`, in the same order. A runner rejects a row whose length differs from `columns`.

allowedDivergence.description: Backends that are ACCEPTED to differ from the result above, each one named and justified (XEQ-4). The point is to make a real, known cross-engine difference visible in the fixture instead of silently passing or silently failing: a backend absent from this list must match `columns`/`rows`, a backend present is held to its own entry instead. At most one entry per backend, or per backend and engine for `search` (XEQ-4).

backend.description: The expected/<backend>.artifact.json stem this entry applies to ('search' is the shared OpenSearch/Elasticsearch artifact, OQ-7).

reason.description: Why the divergence is accepted, citing the rule or the engine fact that causes it (e.g. 'T-SQL rejects a zero-width OFFSET/FETCH window, msg 10744'). A divergence nobody can explain is a bug, not an allowance.

outcome.description: 'rows': the backend returns a different result, given in `expected`. 'error': the backend refuses to execute the query; the harness asserts that it does, so a fix that makes the error disappear is noticed rather than ignored.

expected.description: The result this backend is held to. Required when outcome is 'rows', forbidden when it is 'error'.

engine.description: Only with backend 'search': the shared OpenSearch/Elasticsearch artifact (OQ-7) runs on both engines, and this entry applies to one. Without it, a 'search' entry covers both.
